findings.evidence: Hunk headers `@@ -a,b +c,d @@`: cite new code by the `+c` post-image lines, not working-tree lines.
findings.fix: Shorten to the part the model may get wrong: 'Cite new code by post-image (+) line numbers from the hunk header, not working-tree lines.' The model already knows the unified-diff hunk header format.

findings.evidence: Before writing the report, compare the groups with the selected patch's file list (the manifest, built from the same source: no argument, `git diff HEAD --name-only` plus the untracked list from step 1 ... `custom`, the `diff --git` headers of the pasted patch)
findings.fix: Turn the manifest commands into a short per-source list (no argument / no commits / commit / merge / range or branch / PR / custom), placed after the check sentence. That keeps the validation gate of the process pattern easy to follow instead of hiding it in one long parenthetical.

findings.evidence: Measure size before reading: run `--shortstat` on the same source (for a PR, `gh pr diff "<pr>" --color=never | wc -l`; for `custom`, judge the pasted patch).
findings.fix: For the no-argument source, add the untracked files to the size count, for example: 'plus the line count of each untracked file from step 1, since `--shortstat` omits them'. Without this, a large untracked addition skips the large-diff procedure and runs into the truncation gotcha.
